title: Motion, Animation & Accessibility 🎞️
description: Respect users' preferences for reduced motion and avoid triggering seizures.

slides.title: When Animation Hurts 🤢
slides.content:
For some users, animations can cause:

* **Motion sickness / vertigo** – from parallax, zooming, spinning.
* **Seizures** – from flashing content (>3 flashes per second).
* **Distraction** – ADHD users may lose focus.

WCAG 2.3.1: No content that flashes more than 3 times per second, unless it's below the general flash and red flash thresholds.

quizData.question: What is the maximum allowed flash rate per second to avoid violating WCAG?
quizData.explanation: Content must not flash more than 3 times per second.

slides.title: The `prefers-reduced-motion` Media Query 🧘

quizData.question: When `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` is active, what should you do?

options.text: Do nothing; the browser handles it

quizData.explanation: Your CSS should override animations and transitions, or replace them with subtle opacity fades.

slides.title: Accessible Animation Pattern
slides.content: Use a custom property to control motion:

slides.title: Best Practices for Motion ✅
slides.content:
* **Avoid auto‑playing video or animations** that can't be paused.
* Use **opacity and position** rather than size or rotation for hover effects.
* Keep transitions **short** (under 200ms for interactions).
* Provide a **pause/stop** button for any essential animation.

When in doubt, test with the system setting enabled.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Animate with `transform` and `opacity`
These properties are hardware‑accelerated and cause less jank. Avoid animating `width`, `height`, `top`, `left`.
